label: Node.js + PostgreSQL
summary: Preset: a Node.js application with its own PostgreSQL database; you bring the app. A frontend is built beforehand and shipped as its output (e.g. dist/).

items: Your content is a git branch or an uploaded package. It is inspected, then goes live within about 2 minutes.
If a new release fails inspection or does not answer, the last good release stays live.
Nothing is built on the server: ship everything the app needs in the release. Include `node_modules` and the built frontend (for example `dist/`).
PostgreSQL runs on this container on loopback. `process.env` has `DB_HOST` (`127.0.0.1`), `DB_NAME`, `DB_USER`, `DB_PASSWORD` and `DATABASE_URL`.
Load your schema yourself: ask an administrator, or create the tables from your app on first start.
Files your app writes (uploads) must go in folders listed in `options.dataDirs`: kept across releases and backed up. Every push replaces the release itself.
The app listens on `127.0.0.1:3000` behind Caddy: your start command (default `npm start`) must listen on `$HOST` and `$PORT`.

hint: a Node.js app built on PostgreSQL
